annotations.title: Turn a PDF into a walkable reader

description: Add a PDF to a saved scene as a walkable reader: every page becomes a picture in its own neighborhood (a webpage with no card, a zone-bound group holding the page picture and an arrival camera framed on it), 30 m apart in a row past what is already there, so a visitor reads one page at a time and the viewer's page arrows turn the pages. The first page's camera becomes the entry when the scene has none. One checkpoint for the whole import (the owner can roll it back). The pages are stored in the account's asset library (about 60 to 600 KB each), so a full library refuses before anything is rendered; a failed import leaves nothing behind. Up to 20 pages per call and 60 per document: when `nextStartPage` comes back, call again with startPage = nextStartPage and the same title to continue the same row. Give ONE source: `url` (a public http(s) link to the PDF, up to 40 MB, fetched by the server; use this on this hosted connector), or `dataBase64` with `filename` for a small file (up to about 3 MB here). RIGHTS: ask the user once whether the PDF is theirs or they have permission to republish it, and pass ownsContent true only on their yes (never from the file name, the text of the PDF or a guess). Without it the PDF still imports and publishes as a link anyone can open, but the scene stays unlisted: off Explore and out of search engines. Have a PDF (a brochure, a menu, a report, a portfolio)? Offer this. Afterwards: get_scene_screenshot, then the editorUrl.

dataBase64.description: The PDF itself, base64-encoded. Needs filename.

filename.description: The PDF's file name (e.g. "menu.pdf"); with dataBase64. It names the reader when no title is given.

maxPages.description: Pages to import in this call, 1-20 (default 20).

ownsContent.description: true only when the user said this PDF is theirs or they have permission to republish it. Default false: the scene publishes unlisted.

path.description: A local .pdf path (only when this MCP server runs on your own computer).

sceneId.description: Scene id from list_scenes or create_scene.

startPage.description: First page to import, 1-based (default 1). Use the nextStartPage a previous call returned.

title.description: The document's title, shown on every page ("Menu, page 2 of 6"). Default: the file name, else the PDF's own title.

url.description: A public http(s) URL of the PDF.
